questions.question: Article 368 of the Constitution of India is related to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the** **__**Constitutional amendment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 368 of the Constitution of India mentions two types of amendments to the Indian Constitution.**
 
• One type of amendment is** by a special majority of Parliament **(Lok sabha and Rajya sabha) and the second type of amendment is** by a special majority of the Parliament with the ratification by half of the total states.**
 
• But, some other articles provide for the amendment of certain provisions of the Constitution by a simple majority of the members of each House present and voting (Similar to the ordinary legislative process).
 
• **Notably, these amendments are not deemed to be amendments to the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Procedures:**

 
 
• Article 48 in the Constitution of India is related to agriculture and animal husbandry.
 
• This article come under Part 4 which is the Directive Principle of State Policy.
 
 
 
• **Parliament:**
 
 
• It comes between Articles 79 and 122 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It consists of the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha.
 
 
 
• **​Center-state relation:**
 
 
• Articles 264 to 293 of Part Xii of the Constitution deal with financial relations between the Centre and the state.
 
• Since India is a federal country, it follows the separation of powers relating to taxes and it is the duty of the centre to allocate funds to the states.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides Fundamental Duties?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **42ⁿd Amendment Act of 1976 added to Fundamental Duties to the Indian Constitution 86th Amendment Act 2002 later added 11th Fundamental duty to the list.**
 
• **Swaran singh committee in 1976 recommended fundamental duties**, the necessity of which was felt during the internal emergency of 1975-77.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are dealt with** Article 51A under Part-IV a of the Indian Constitution.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 18:**

 
 
• It talks about the **abolition of titles.**
 
• It says: No title, not being a military or academic distinction, shall be conferred by the state.
 
 
 
• **Article 81:**
 
 
• It defines the composition of the **House of the people or Lok Sabha.**
 
• It states that the House shall not consist of more than 550 elected members of whom not more than 20 will represent Union Territories.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A:**
 
 
• The constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002 inserted Article 21 A in the constitution of India to provide free and compulsory education of all children in the age group of six to fourteen years as a fundamental right in such a manner as the state may, by law.

questions.question: The Hazarduari Palace is located in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Murshidabad.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Hazarduari Palace is a landmark of sizable importance in **Murshidabad, West Bengal.**
 
• The palace was given to the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) for preservation in 1985 and sprawls over a huge area.**
 
• Hazarduari Palace was earlier called **Bara Kothi and lies within the Kila Nizamat campus.**
 
• It lies near the Ganga River's bank and was built in the 19th century by the famous architect **Duncan Macleod**, during the reign of Nawab Nazim Humayun Jah who ruled Bengal, Orissa, and Bihar from 1824 to 1838.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Archaeological Survey of India:**

 
 
• It is an attached agency of the **Ministry of Culture of the Government of India**.
 
• It engages in archaeological research and conservation, and protection and preservation of ancient monuments and archaeological sites in the country.
 
• ASI regulates all archaeological activities conducted in the country through the provisions of the **Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act (AMASR Act), 1958.**
 
• It also regulates the **Antiquities and Art Treasure Act, 1972.**

questions.question: Tea and Coffee are grown in _______ soil.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Laterite**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Laterite soils are very suitable for tea, espresso and cashew cultivation.
 
• **Laterite soils lack fertility due to intensive leaching.**
 
• When manured and irrigated, some Laterite are fantastic for developing the plantation floras like tea,coffee, rubber, cinchona, coconut, areca nut, etc,
 
• **Tea and coffee crops demand evenly distributed rainfall and no problems of water logging.**
 
• The hill slopes provide an easy drainage for rain water and helps to prevent water logging. 
 
• The** tea and coffee plantations grow well in loamy soil that is found in large quantities on the hill slopes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• It is widespread in the northern plains and river valleys.
 
• It covers about 40% of the total land area of the country.
 
 
 
• **Black Soil:**
 
 
• It is also known as **'Regur Soil**' or the Black cotton Soil.
 
• It covers most of the Deccan Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Arid Soil:**
 
 
• It is also known as desert soil.
 
• It is primarily found in the parts of Haryana, Western Rajasthan, and Punjab, and elongates up to the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat.

questions.question: Sorters in the Wool industry sometimes get infected by a bacterium called ______, which causes a fatal blood disease called ‘Sorter’s Disease’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anthrax.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Anthrax causes a fatal blood disease known as sorter's disease.**
 
• It is a rare infectious disease caused by the **bacterium Bacillus anthracis.**
 
• It occurs naturally around the world in** wild and domestic hoofed animals, especially cattle, sheep, goats, camels, and antelopes.**
 
• It can also occur in humans when they are exposed to the bacterium, usually through handling animals or animals' hides.
 
• There are **3 forms of anthrax infection: cutaneous (skin), inhalation (lungs), and gastrointestinal (stomach and intestine)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetobacter pasteurianus:**

 
 
• It is an acetic acid-producing bacterium commonly found associated with plants and plant products.
 
• This organism is used in the production of fermented foods, such as kefir, and vinegar.
 
 
 
• **Edwardsiella:**
 
 
• It is a genus of gram-negative, fermentation bacteria of the family **Hafniaceae**.
 
• It was first discovered in snakes in 1962.
 
 
 
• **Melittangium boletus:**
 
 
• ​It is a mesophilic proteobacterium that builds a fruiting body and was isolated from soil with rotting wood.

questions.question: Which of the following newspapers was started by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sambad Kumudi.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raja Rammohan Roy was one of the founders of the Brahmo Sabha, the precursor of the Brahmo Samaj, which was a social-religious reform movement in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• He had started two newspapers- one in Bangali, which was known as the Sambad kumudi, and another in Persian, which was called the Mirat-ul-Akbar.
 
• Given below refers to a brief description of the two newspapers:
 
 
• **Sambad Kumudi:**
 
 
• It referred to a **Bengali weekly newspaper** that was published in Kolkata during the first half of the 19th century by Ram Mohan Roy.
 
• It mentioned a noted pro-reformist publication that had actively campaigned for the abolition (stop) of the Sati Pratha.
 
 
 
• **Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Mirror of News):**
 
 
• It referred to a** Persian language** journal rant that was founded as well as edited by Raja Rammohan Roy.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amrita Bazar Patrika:**

 
 
• It was published on** 20 February 1868** by two brothers in the undivided Bengal's Jessore district.
 
• It shut down in **1991**.
 
 
 
• **Karmayogin:**
 
 
• It was originally published in the nationalist newspaper Karmayogin between June 1909 and February 1910.
 
• It was published by **Sri Aurobindo**.
 
 
 
• **Ananda Bazar Patrika:**
 
 
• It is an Indian Bengali-language daily newspaper owned by the ABP Group.
 
• It was published on **1922**.

questions.question: Krishnadevaraya, who reigned over Vijayanagar from 1509 to 1529, belonged to the:
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Sri Krishnadeva Raya was the most illustrious king of the Vijayanagar Empire.**
 
• He **belonged to the Taluva dynasty.**
 
• When he** ascended the throne in 1509, **the affair of the Empire was in a gloomy state.
 
• The sultan of Bijapur and the rulers of Orissa were a constant threat to the empire.
 
• He defeated the combined Muslim forces of Deccan Sultanates and captured **Raichur Doab** in** 1512 AD**.
 
• He maintained** friendly relations with the Portuguese.**
 
• Besides being a great warrior, he was an able administrator and a liberal patron of art and literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This dynasty's rulers were the rulers of northern Karnataka in modern India.
 
• This dynasty was ruled by three kings from 1485 to 1505.
 
 
• Saluva Narasimha
 
• Thimma Bhupala
 
• Narasimha Raya II
 
 
 
 
 
• **Sangama Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Sangama dynasty was a dynasty of the **Vijayanagara Empire** founded in the 14th century by two brothers: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I.

questions.question: The play 'Abhijnana Shakuntalam' by Kalidasa is a love story between Shakuntala and King _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Dushyanta.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhigyan Shakuntalam is an excellent drama by Mahakavi Kalidas**.
 
• It has been acclaimed** internationally.**
 
• It consists of **seven acts that deal with the well-known love story of king Dushyant and the maiden Shakuntala.**
 
• This love story has been presented artistically.
 
• It is **a pictorial presentation of human feelings.**
 
• It is an excellent** presentation of human love and natural love**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalidas:**

 
 
• He was **a Sanskrit author who is often considered ancient India's greatest poet and playwright.**
 
• His plays and poetry are primarily based on the Vedas, the Mahabharata, and the Purana.
 
• He is still remembered because as Kalidas was a writer, he also wrote many moral poems, also the most popular in most of the region.
